steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: British film narrative has distinctive traditions that differ from Hollywood's classical model, often prioritising social observation, character study and realism over goal-driven plot mechanics. | Key Fact: Social realism is a defining tradition in British cinema, presenting working-class life with authenticity, political awareness and a commitment to representing experiences that mainstream cinema typically ignores. | Key Fact: The kitchen sink tradition of the late 1950s and 1960s brought working-class domestic life to British screens with unprecedented frankness, challenging the middle-class conventions of earlier British cinema. | Key Fact: British narratives often resist the classical Hollywood drive towards resolution, instead favouring open endings, unresolved conflicts a
